newsitem.title: UK: SNOOKER-O'SULLIVAN OUT OF WORLD CHAMPIONSHIP.
newsitem.headline: SNOOKER-O'SULLIVAN OUT OF WORLD CHAMPIONSHIP.

text.p: Englishman Ronnie O'Sullivan, who made a maximum 147 break in the first round, was knocked out of the world championship 13-12 by Welshman Darren Morgan on Saturday.

Morgan had trailed 9-7 overnight in the second round clash but kept O'Sullivan off the table for long periods. The 21-year-old eighth seed failed to sink a ball in either of the opening two frames as Morgan produced his third century break of the match, a 116, to take the opener 132-0, and then a run of 59 carried him to the next 77-0.
O'Sullivan got on the board by taking the next frame, and he had chances in the 20th to restore his two-frame advantage, but it was Morgan who took it with a 63 clearance to make it 10-10.
Morgan's 40 break in the next took him to 11-10, and there was real drama in the next when they finished level at 61-61 and the black had to be re-spotted.
Morgan doubled it in to require only one of the last three frames for victory, but O'Sullivan showed his fighting spirit by winning the next two 84-44 and 89-39.
The Welshman was not to be denied, however, and compiled a painstaking break of 84 without reply to clinch victory in the decider.
Meanwhile French-Canadian Alain Robidoux extended his advantage from 5-3 to 8-5 against giant-killer Stefan Mazrocis.
Robidoux took the first three frames of Saturday's session 61-55, 57-32 and 66-1, but Mazrocis bounced back to win the next two, 63-50 and 89-39.
